2027-04-01.title: First Thursday of Resurrection
2027-04-01.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The election of the seven deacons
Jesus sends out his twelve disciples
2027-04-01.alt: Season of the Resurrection (Qyamta). The first week of the Resurrection, the week of the newly baptised. The calendar notes the fuller passages: Isaiah 54:1–15 and Colossians 2:8–3:4. Since the Monday after Hosanna Sunday the Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Mar Addai and Mar Mari.
2027-04-01.verse: Cure the sick, raise the dead, cleanse the lepers, cast out demons. You received without payment; give without payment.
theo: Five days after Easter the Church hears a song addressed to a woman who has no children. “Sing, O barren one who did not bear; burst into song and shout, you who have not been in labor! For the children of the desolate woman will be more than the children of her that is married, says the LORD.” Isaiah was speaking to Jerusalem in exile, a city that looked finished, a mother with an empty house. And God tells her to start building extensions: “Enlarge the site of your tent, and let the curtains of your habitations be stretched out; do not hold back; lengthen your cords and strengthen your stakes.” Children are coming whom she never expected. Paul reads this song as a word about the Church (Galatians 4:26–27), and the Easter liturgy reads it this week for a reason. On the night of the Resurrection the font gave birth to new sons and daughters; the Church that seemed so small on Good Friday, a handful of women and one disciple at the Cross, now has to widen her tent. The heart of the passage is the tenderness of God: “For a brief moment I abandoned you, but with great compassion I will gather you.” And he binds himself with the oath he swore to Noah: “For the mountains may depart and the hills be removed, but my steadfast love shall not depart from you, and my covenant of peace shall not be removed, says the LORD, who has compassion on you.” Whatever moment of abandonment we have passed through, Easter says it was a brief moment. The steadfast love remains.

The tent grows, and growth brings trouble. In Acts the community in Jerusalem has become large and mixed: Greek-speaking believers and Aramaic-speaking believers, all of them Jews who believe in Jesus. “The Hellenists complained against the Hebrews because their widows were being neglected in the daily distribution of food.” The apostles do not deny the problem or tell the complainers to be quiet. They gather the whole community and make a decision that will shape the Church for ever. “It is not right that we should neglect the word of God in order to wait on tables. Therefore, friends, select from among yourselves seven men of good standing, full of the Spirit and of wisdom, whom we may appoint to this task, while we, for our part, will devote ourselves to prayer and to serving the word.” The seven are chosen, all with Greek names, from the very group that felt neglected; the apostles pray and lay hands on them. The Church has always seen here the beginning of the diaconate. And the result? “The word of God continued to spread; the number of the disciples increased greatly in Jerusalem, and a great many of the priests became obedient to the faith.” Care for widows and the preaching of the word are not rivals; when the poor are served, the word runs faster. Paul tells the Colossians where this new life comes from: “when you were buried with him in baptism, you were also raised with him through faith in the power of God, who raised him from the dead.” God has cancelled our debt, “erasing the record that stood against us with its legal demands. He set this aside, nailing it to the cross.” On the Cross Christ “disarmed the rulers and authorities and made a public example of them, triumphing over them in it.” The newly baptised do not have to fight their old masters in their own strength. The battle has already been won.

The Gospel takes us back to the beginning of the mission. “Then Jesus summoned his twelve disciples and gave them authority over unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to cure every disease and every sickness.” Matthew lists them by name, and among them, in the pair “Thomas and Matthew the tax collector”, is the apostle whom the Christians of Kerala call their father in faith. Jesus gives them a message and a manner. The message: “As you go, proclaim the good news, ‘The kingdom of heaven has come near.’” The manner: “You received without payment; give without payment.” They are to travel without gold, without a bag, without a spare tunic, depending on the welcome of those who receive them. They bring peace into houses: “As you enter the house, greet it. If the house is worthy, let your peace come upon it.” Read in Easter week, this Gospel reminds us that the mission did not begin after the Resurrection; it was rehearsed in Galilee, and the Risen Lord now gives it its full meaning. What the apostles received without payment was, in the end, life from the dead. Every Christian has received the same: forgiveness, Baptism, the Body and Blood of the Lord, none of it earned. So everything we give, our time to a lonely widow, our money to the poor, our word of faith to a doubting friend, is only the overflow of what was given to us without payment. A Church that charges for grace has forgotten Easter; a Church that gives freely is preaching the Resurrection without saying a word.
conn: “Sing, O barren one who did not bear” (Isaiah 54:1); Hannah sings when the barren woman bears (1 Samuel 2:5); Paul applies Isaiah's song to the Jerusalem above, “and she is our mother” (Galatians 4:26–27).

God set his bow in the clouds as a sign of the covenant (Genesis 9:13); he swears by the days of Noah that his steadfast love will not depart (Isaiah 54:9–10); Peter sees in the flood a figure of Baptism (1 Peter 3:20–21).
Seven helpers full of the Spirit.

Moses was given seventy elders to share the burden, with the spirit that was on him (Numbers 11:16–17); the apostles are given seven men full of the Spirit and of wisdom (Acts 6:3); Paul names the qualities of deacons (1 Timothy 3:8–13).
God is “Father of orphans and protector of widows” (Psalm 68:5); pure religion is “to care for orphans and widows in their distress” (James 1:27).
“we have been buried with him by baptism into death” (Romans 6:4); “you were also raised with him through faith” (Colossians 2:12).
Jesus calls the Twelve and sends them out two by two (Mark 6:7); after the Resurrection he sends them to all nations (Matthew 28:19–20).
altar: At every Holy Qurbana the deacon stands between the altar and the people, calling us to prayer, to attention and to peace. His service at the altar is the same service the seven gave at the tables of the widows: the Lord who feeds us asks us to feed others.
Nothing on the altar is bought. The bread and wine we offer become, by the Holy Spirit, the true Body and Blood of Christ, given to us without payment. We receive freely so that we may give freely.
outline: A widow in a back pew whom nobody has visited since the funeral.
The barren one sings: Easter makes the Church a mother of many.
Point 2 · Seven men full of the Spirit
Serving tables and serving the word.
The record against us erased; the powers disarmed.
The Twelve sent with empty bags and full hands.
The seven kneeling while the apostles lay hands on them.
“You received without payment; give without payment.”
live: This week visit, telephone or bring food to one widow or widower in your family or parish who may feel forgotten.
Do one service this week for which you will receive no payment and no thanks.
Pray today for the deacons and the seminarians of your eparchy, and for one young man you know who may be called.
Find the date of your Baptism, and on that day each year light a candle and thank God.
fathers: Christ sent the apostles without gold or bag so that their very poverty would preach. Freed from all anxiety about food and clothing, they could give themselves wholly to the word, and the people who saw them could not suspect them of seeking gain. He gave them the power to raise the dead and told them to give it freely, so that their gift would match the gift they had received.

The barren woman who is told to sing is the Church gathered from the nations. She who seemed to have no children now gives birth every year in the font, and she has more children than the synagogue of old, not by human strength but by the grace of God who makes the barren a joyful mother.
magis: Deacons are ordained not to the priesthood but to the ministry; they serve at the altar, in the proclamation of the Gospel and in works of charity.
Jesus called the Twelve and sent them; the apostles are the envoys of Christ, and their mission continues in the Church.
Baptism signifies the descent into the tomb of the Christian, who dies to sin with Christ in order to live a new life.
God blesses those who come to the aid of the poor; the Church's love for the poor is part of her constant tradition.
The New Law is called a law of love, a law of grace and a law of freedom.
saints: Thursday 1 April is the First Thursday of Resurrection. Tomorrow, Friday 2 April, the Syro-Malabar calendar keeps the Feast of Martyrs, in the East Syriac tradition the commemoration of all the saints (verify locally). Sunday 4 April: New Sunday (Puthu Njayar).
2027-04-01.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, risen from the dead, you widen the tent of your Church and give her children she never expected. Thank you for the grace we received without payment: our Baptism, your forgiveness, your Body and Blood. Make us generous with what we have received. Bless the deacons of your Church and all who serve at the tables of the poor; let no widow be neglected among us. Send us, as you sent the Twelve, to bring your peace into every house we enter. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Isaiah: sing, O barren one; enlarge your tent; my steadfast love shall not depart from you.
Acts: seven men full of the Spirit are chosen to serve the neglected widows, and the word of God spreads.
Jesus sends the Twelve: you received without payment; give without payment.
2027-04-01.action: Visit or call one widow or widower today who may feel forgotten.
2027-04-01.question: What have I received freely from God, and what am I giving freely in return?
kidsaint: Philip was one of the seven men chosen to help the apostles care for the poor. Later he went to Samaria to preach about Jesus, and on a desert road he met an important official from Ethiopia reading the prophet Isaiah in his chariot. Philip explained the reading, and the man was baptised in water by the roadside. Lesson: a helper at the table can also be a teller of the Good News!
2027-04-01.special: First Thursday of Resurrection. Easter week, the week of the newly baptised.
term: The Syriac word for a deacon, meaning ‘one who serves’; in Malayalam, Shemmashan. Deacons are ordained to serve at the altar, to proclaim the Gospel and to care for the poor, as the seven did in Acts 6.

family.explain: Jesus chose twelve friends and sent them out to tell people that God's kingdom was near. He gave them power to heal the sick. Then he told them: you got all this as a gift, so give it away as a gift! God has given us many gifts without asking anything back: our life, our family, his love, Baptism. We can give without asking anything back too: help at home without being asked, share a toy, be kind to someone who is lonely.
family.intention: We pray that our family may share freely the gifts God has given us.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing I can do for someone this week without wanting anything back?”

illus: In a parish near Changanacherry the youth group ran the Easter food-kit distribution. Every family on the list received a kit. On the Thursday after Easter a girl in the group noticed an old woman sitting alone after the Holy Qurbana. She was a widow from a family that had moved from Tamil Nadu for work years ago; her name had never been put on the list, because no one in the parish committee knew her. Nobody had meant to forget her. The girl told the vicar, and he did not scold anyone. He called the youth together, read Acts 6 with them, and asked two of them to visit her every week. ‘The apostles had this problem in the first month of the Church,’ he said. ‘The answer was not a new rule. It was people full of the Spirit who would go and see.’ By Pentecost the widow was teaching the children a Tamil hymn to Our Lady.

pm.open: Risen Lord, you have given us everything without payment. Open our hands to give, and our hearts to welcome. Amen. Alleluia!
share: Enlarge the site of your tent (Isaiah 54:2). Whom is God asking me to make room for?
Their widows were being neglected (Acts 6:1). Who is being overlooked in my family or parish?
He set this aside, nailing it to the cross (Colossians 2:14). Do I still carry guilt that Christ has already erased?
You received without payment; give without payment (Matthew 10:8). What can I give freely this week?
interc: For the deacons and seminarians of our eparchy, that they may be full of the Spirit and of wisdom.
For widows, widowers and the elderly who live alone, that the Church may never neglect them.
For the newly baptised, that they may live as people raised with Christ.
For migrants and those who worship far from their home, that they may find a welcome in our parishes.
For all who are sent to proclaim the Gospel, that they may bring peace into every house.
pm.close: Father, you made the barren one sing and widened the tent of your people. Keep us in your steadfast love, fill us with your Spirit, and send us to give freely what we have freely received. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

homily: Dear friends, Isaiah sings to a woman with an empty house: “Sing, O barren one… Enlarge the site of your tent.” This week the Church is that woman. On Good Friday she was a few women and one disciple at the Cross. On Easter night the font gave her new children. Now God says: make room, there are more coming.

And God adds a promise: “For a brief moment I abandoned you, but with great compassion I will gather you… my steadfast love shall not depart from you.” If you have been through a dark time, hear this: it was a brief moment. His love has not moved.

But a bigger family brings bigger problems. In Acts the Greek-speaking widows are being forgotten at the daily meal. The apostles listen. They do not say, ‘Stop complaining.’ They ask the community to choose seven men full of the Spirit and of wisdom, and they lay hands on them. These are the first deacons. And the word of God spreads even faster.

Paul tells us where the strength comes from. In Baptism we were buried with Christ and raised with him. God erased the record that stood against us, “nailing it to the cross.” The powers that held us are disarmed. We do not serve out of fear. We serve as children of God, no longer slaves.

Then Jesus sends the Twelve, Thomas among them, with nothing in their bags. “You received without payment; give without payment.” Everything we have from God is a gift: our life, our faith, the Holy Qurbana we receive every Sunday. Nobody paid for it.

So this week let us give something without payment. Visit one widow. Do one job with no thanks. Pray for our deacons and seminarians. A Church that gives freely is the best sermon on the Resurrection. Christ is risen! Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus told his friends: ‘You got it as a gift, so give it as a gift!’ God gives us so many presents: our family, our food, his love.
This week, give a present of kindness: help someone without being asked, and do not ask for anything back.

intro: Theme: “You received without payment; give without payment.”
The barren one who sings, the seven who serve, the record nailed to the Cross, and the Twelve sent out with empty bags.

points.h: My steadfast love shall not depart
sub: A brief moment, an everlasting love.
q: For the mountains may depart and the hills be removed, but my steadfast love shall not depart from you, and my covenant of peace shall not be removed, says the LORD, who has compassion on you.

For I am convinced that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor rulers, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers, nor height, nor depth, nor anything else in all creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus our Lord.
points.apply: Name one dark time you have come through, and thank God that his love did not move.

points.h: Seven men full of the Spirit
q: I will take some of the spirit that is on you and put it on them; and they shall bear the burden of the people along with you so that you will not bear it all by yourself.
Therefore, friends, select from among yourselves seven men of good standing, full of the Spirit and of wisdom, whom we may appoint to this task.
points.apply: Find out who in your parish is being overlooked, and go and see them.

q: I am going to open your graves, and bring you up from your graves, O my people.
when you were buried with him in baptism, you were also raised with him through faith in the power of God, who raised him from the dead.
points.apply: Bring to the Sacrament of Reconciliation the guilt you still carry, and leave it at the Cross.

q: Since there will never cease to be some in need on the earth, I therefore command you, “Open your hand to the poor and needy neighbor in your land.”
You received without payment; give without payment.
points.apply: Do one act of service this week for which you will receive nothing back.

concl: The Risen Lord widens the tent of his Church, erases our debt and sends us out with empty bags and full hands.
What we received without payment we give without payment, and the word of God spreads.
2027-04-01.resolve: This week, visit one widow or widower, pray for the deacons and seminarians of your eparchy, and do one hidden service without payment.
